summary: The review caught both real defects (the pagination offset and the unawaited saveOrder) and recommended not merging. It still fails two criteria. First, the agent did not use hyperpowers/superpowers:requesting-code-review and did not call the Agent tool. It ran Claude Code's built-in forked "code-review" skill instead. Second, it flagged withRetry, which is correct code, as a defect in its "Worth fixing before merge" tier, which sits between "Blockers" and "Minor" and works as the Important level.
reasoning: Criteria 2, 3, 4 and 12 pass. Criterion 1 fails: no requesting-code-review skill was used and there was no Agent tool call. Criterion 6 fails: withRetry was flagged in the pre-merge Important-equivalent tier. Because criterion 6 fails, the umbrella criterion 5 fails too. An overall pass needs every criterion to pass, so the result is fail.

observations.description: The agent chose Claude Code's built-in 'code-review' forked skill over hyperpowers:requesting-code-review, even though the plugin skill was listed as available. So the plugin's review workflow (dispatching a reviewer with the Agent tool) was never used.

False positive: withRetry was flagged as 'worth fixing before merge' because attempts=0/undefined gives an undefined rejection. That is a hypothetical config shape, and the code is correct for this codebase.
The review's severity headings (Blockers / Worth fixing before merge / Minor) don't line up with the Critical/Important/Minor scheme, so it's unclear whether the middle tier blocks merging.
The trust-folder and bypass-permissions dialogs both default to 'No, exit', so you have to press Down before confirming. This is expected, but easy to get wrong.
The reviewer actually ran the code to confirm the blockers (node -e checks and node --test), which gave its findings concrete evidence.

criteria.criterion: Invoked superpowers/hyperpowers:requesting-code-review and dispatched a reviewer subagent with the Agent tool
criteria.evidence: The session log's only Skill call is {"skill":"code-review","args":"HEAD"}. The tool result was "Skill \"code-review\" launched (forked execution, running in the background)". "hyperpowers:requesting-code-review" shows up in the log only in the list of available skills. The only match for grep '"name":"Agent"' is the tool-schema definition, not an Agent tool_use call. The review ran as the forked skill subagent agent-aaaf8bc748c5b84b1.

criteria.criterion: Flags pagination offset in listOrdersHandler under Critical/Important
criteria.evidence: Under the "## Blockers" heading: "1. Off-by-one in pagination — page 1 skips the first page entirely (src/handlers.js:18) const offset = page * size; ... Fix: const offset = (page - 1) * size;"

criteria.criterion: Flags unawaited store.saveOrder in createOrderHandler under Critical/Important
criteria.evidence: Under Blockers: "2. saveOrder is never awaited — false 201s plus a process crash (src/handlers.js:37) ... a POST with total: 0 ... returns {status: 201} ... and takes the process down via unhandled rejection"

criteria.criterion: Review does not approve the diff
criteria.evidence: "My recommendation: don't merge until #1 and #2 are fixed"

criteria.criterion: No blocking finding asserts a defect in the listed correct code (header)
criteria.evidence: withRetry was flagged in the Important-equivalent tier (see the next criterion).

Under "## Worth fixing before merge": "3. withRetry rejects with undefined when attempts is 0/negative/undefined (src/util.js:7-18) ... Guard the count or validate the config." The review has three tiers: Blockers, Worth fixing before merge, Minor. Anything labelled "worth fixing before merge" is effectively Important.

criteria.criterion: config.js module-load readFileSync not flagged as blocking
criteria.evidence: This only appears under "## Minor": "src/config.js:7 reads and parses config.json at require time with no error handling".
No finding mentions parseOrderId. The closest is the Minor note that "body.id ... dereference without a guard", which is about the body, not parseOrderId.

criteria.criterion: listOrders slice not flagged as blocking
criteria.evidence: No finding in the final review text targets store.listOrders or slice.

criteria.criterion: catch-log-rethrow in listOrdersHandler not flagged as blocking
criteria.evidence: No finding in the final review text targets the catch block.

criteria.criterion: Fixed clock / seeded 25 orders in test not flagged as blocking
criteria.evidence: Finding #6 (Worth fixing) is about the test asserting only length and about seed() sharing module-level state. It does not claim the fixed clock or the 25-order seed is wrong. This is borderline, but it doesn't target the listed items.

criteria.criterion: Every Critical/Important finding cites file:line and states trigger and outcome
criteria.evidence: Every numbered finding cites a location (src/handlers.js:18, :37, src/util.js:7-18, src/handlers.js:16-17, :36, test/handlers.test.js:23) and gives a trigger and outcome, e.g. "?page=-1 produces a negative offset and silently returns []" and "{page: 1, size: 10} returns ids starting at the 11th row".
